CAMERA CAVEAT, so it is not miscounted as a movement win: the shake rewrite (coherent two-sine noise, roll term, offset undone before the lerp, single decay at player.js:1274) is genuinely fixed and framerate-independent, but nothing movement-driven raises camShake — the only sources are SHOT_SHAKE on fire (fx.js:170), explosions (fx.js:233) and being hit (fx.js:264). justification:
The prior verdict rested on one sentence: "pulling the trigger produces no camera kick, no view-model movement, no FOV punch and no hitstop, and camShake is written in exactly two places, neither of which is your own gun." That is now false on every clause, verified in code.

FIRING KICK — fx.js:94-95 defines SHOT_SHAKE {pistol .06, smg .045, ar .07, shotgun .20, sniper .26, glauncher .18} and SHOT_FOV {2, 2, 2.5, 5, 5, 4.5}; fx.js:169-172 raises both, gated `if (a === W.player)` so the other 49 actors' shots do not shake you. VIEW-MODEL — weapons.js:439 sets `a.vmKick = 1` on every fire, consumed at weapons.js:271-274 as `weaponMesh.position.z = -vmKick*0.05` decaying at 6/s = a 5 cm slide over 167 ms; nothing else writes weaponMesh.position (only player.js:750, a visibility LOD that explicitly exempts the local player), so it is live.

SHAKE QUALITY — player.js:1256-1268 replaced per-frame `Math.random()` with two incommensurate sine sums (41.3/27.1 and 33.7/19.9 rad/s) plus a roll term `nx*s*0.11` applied after `lookAt` (which zeroes roll), so the shotgun's 0.20 now reads as 1.26° of roll rather than framerate-dependent buzz. The double decay is genuinely gone: `grep -rn "camShake" runtime/` returns setters in fx.js and exactly one decay, player.js:1274, running AFTER the apply.

HITSTOP — ffg_royale3d.js:493-496 scales the frame step to 0.12x while `W.hitstopT > 0`, decremented with the real dt so the freeze is wall-clock constant; fired from fx.js:272 (own kill, 50 ms), :249 (headshot, 30 ms), :234 (explosion within 8 m, 70 ms). Solo only (`if (!W.net)`).

HIT FLASH — this is the item the prompt flagged as previously inert, and it is now real. player.js:284-285 adds a `zFlash` uniform and player.js:292 multiplies it into `diffuseColor.rgb`; fx.js:150-151 captures `material.userData.zFlash` and fx.js:435 drives it. The old `.color` path was algebraically cancelled by the zone-tint shader (which divides `diffuse` back out) — fx.js:147-149 documents that it "shipped invisible on 100% of actors". ffg_royale3d.js:388 warms the whole scene with compileAsync before the lobby, so the uniform exists on every actor material before first contact.

EXPLOSIONS — fx.js:102-124 builds a pooled 4-slot additive flash sprite + flat RingGeometry shockwave; fx.js:410-423 ramps the sprite to R*2.2 over 90 ms and the ring to R*1.6 over 250 ms. No PointLight, deliberately.

PERMANENCE — fx.js:177-183 ejects one brass casing (0xc9a227, 4.5 cm, 1.5 s) per trigger pull, correctly once per fire() not once per pellet; player.js:1368-1375 replaced the one-frame corpse pop with a 3 s hold then a 1.2 s tween sinking the body 1.6 m; loot.js:541 gives death-drop loot the chest glow sprite at scale 1.3.

Plus: red 40 px kill-confirm hitmarker for 280 ms with the head-priority latch cleared (hud.js:2374-2380); hurt vignette now scaled `clamp(dmg/60, 0.3, 1)` (hud.js:2363) instead of a flat 0.4; a persistent low-HP tint ramping under 35 HP (hud.js:1670, 1760) and a critical HP bar that turns #ff5544 and pulses at ≤25 (hud.js:1754-1755); propBreak, hardLand and landed FX listeners that did not exist (fx.js:281-295); non-flesh impact audio that was entirely silent (audio.js:484-500); four per-shot decorrelators so full-auto stops combing (audio.js:280-302); a victory beat that spends the 2600 ms hold on a 0.8 rad/s camera orbit and 1.3 m pull-back (ffg_royale3d.js:482-485 → player.js:1228/1216), four staggered world-space firework bursts (ffg_royale3d.js:431-435 → fx.js:333-335) and the cheer emote; and an OFF/HALF/FULL screen-shake accommodation (hud.js:2985-2992).

Score: 8 of the 11 prior gaps closed, 2 partial, 1 open by design. On Vlambeer's named list the build went from 2 of 6 (muzzle flash, visible bullets) to 5.5 of 6 — kickback, sleep and most of permanence now ship; only decals are missing. The informational layer was already rated commercial-grade, so with the physical layer present and tuned, this reaches parity. It is NOT ahead: the FOV punch is measurably eaten before it renders, there are no bullet decals, no weapon builds a recoil pattern, and online matches get no hitstop at all.

justification:
Score holds at parity; the movement is real but it is entirely in the FEEDBACK layer, and every one of the eight mechanical gaps from the prior entry is untouched or half-touched. Only one commit landed after the prior scorecard (which was committed in 791b7806): f5502ecb, "parity program — 134 edits". Its weapons.js diff is 50 added / 3 removed lines and its sim/royale.js diff is squads-only — no weapon table, no spread function, no hitbox, no fire gate.

WHAT ACTUALLY MOVED (all verified wired end-to-end, not just present):
1. Firing now moves the screen. fx.js:94 SHOT_SHAKE {pistol .06, smg .045, ar .07, shotgun .20, sniper .26, gl .18} and fx.js:95 SHOT_FOV {2,2,2.5,5,5,4.5} are set at fx.js:170-171 gated on `a === W.player`, and BOTH are consumed: shake at player.js:1262 (with the new OFF/HALF/FULL setting, hud.js:2986) and FOV at player.js:1290-1291. Not inert. Because the human's aim ray IS the camera direction (crosshairPoint, weapons.js:353-357), an AR kick of 0.07 m against the 8 m lookAt target is a real ~0.50 deg view displacement — larger than the AR's 0.112 deg ADS first-shot cone — for 2-3 frames.
2. View-model punch: weapons.js:445-ish `a.vmKick = 1` (weapons.js:439) decaying at dt*6 into a 5 cm slide down the barrel axis (weapons.js:271-273). The proto wrapper Group is built at origin (weapons.js:181-182), so the absolute write to position.z is a genuine 5 cm displacement, not a snap-to-zero. Not inert.
3. Hitstop shipped: 0.07 s within 8 m of a blast (fx.js:234), 0.03 s on your own headshot (fx.js:249), 0.05 s on your own kill (fx.js:272), consumed as `step *= 0.12` at ffg_royale3d.js:493-496.
4. The enemy hit flash, which was the prior "shipped but inert" case, now renders. fx.js:151 reads material.userData.zFlash; the uniform exists (player.js:284-285) and is multiplied through the zone-tint fragment shader (player.js:292), so it survives the `diffuseColor.rgb / max(vec3(0.0001), diffuse)` division that used to cancel the old .color animation algebraically.
5. camShake double-decay fixed — fx.js's copy removed, decay lives only at player.js:1274 (dt*1.8). Durations restored: AR 39 ms, sniper 144 ms, explosion 283 ms.
6. Whiz-by cue (weapons.js:521-530, 3.5 m closest-approach, `p.whizzed` correctly reset on pool reuse) + audio (audio.js:505-520, 3200→1200 Hz bandpass, 60 ms throttle). Brass casing per trigger pull (fx.js:176-182). Hurt vignette now scales with damage — hud.js:2363 `opacity = clamp(dmg/60, 0.3, 1)`, was binary. Red 40 px kill-confirm hitmarker for 280 ms with both latches cleared (hud.js:2373-2380).

Net: the trigger now does something (that was the loudest complaint and it is genuinely fixed), but the mechanical skill layer under it — recoil to control, a spray penalty, a hitbox strafing can beat, flinch — is exactly where it was. Parity, improved, not ahead. Standing caveat carried forward from the prior entry: Final Drop's combat internals are not published anywhere reachable, so this is scored against the Fortnite lineage it demonstrably derives from, not against measured Final Drop numbers.

justification:
Four of the prior entry's ten gaps closed, none regressed, so the dimension improved and stays ahead — but "ahead" describes the AI system's DEPTH, not how hard the game plays, and the single largest difficulty lever named in the prior score is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Baseline check first: the prior scorecard was committed AT 791b7806 but was authored against the code BEFORE it (verified: `git show 88941301:...bots.js` line 165 is exactly the HEAL line the prior gap quotes, and line 567 is `const aimY = tp.y + 1.15 + (seen ? (t.vel ? 0 : 0) : 0)` — the flat aim point it quotes). So both 791b7806 and the f5502ecb parity program count as "since". bots.js itself moved only 13 lines in the parity program (`git diff 791b7806 HEAD --stat` → bots.js 13 +/-); everything else bot-facing landed in 791b7806.

WHAT MOVED (verified):
1. Bots can land headshots now. bots.js:581 `HEAD_CHANCE = [0, 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.25]`, rolled per-target (bots.js:592) and per-burst (bots.js:689); bots.js:641-642 `const th = t.swimming ? 0.9 : K.actorHeight(t); const aimY = tp.y + th * (bb.aimHigh ? 0.94 : 0.64)`. Standing 1.8 m target → 1.692 m, against weapons.js:544 `isHead = py > feetY + (headY - feetY) * 0.86 && dh < 0.2` = 1.548 m. The old 1.15 m point sat 0.4 m below that threshold and could not reach it at any tier. It is crouch-aware (K.actorHeight shrinks to 1.548 m via royale.js:133) and swim-aware, so it holds at every stance. Tiers 1-2 stay at 0 — the low end of the curve is deliberately preserved.
2. Supply drops are contested. bots.js:57-65 subscribes to `supplyDropLanded` (emitted loot.js:284) and marks any brain within 220 m; bots.js:216-218 scores `s.SUPPLY` at 58 base / 78 for loot_goblin minus 0.12/m, expiring at 90 s; onEnter at bots.js:298, actSupply at bots.js:501-506, dispatch at bots.js:413. The mark is cleared on arrival within 4 m so a bot that gets there second does not orbit empty grass. loot.js's own "contested by nobody" comment is gone.
3. Crouch is wired and not inert. Reset per frame at bots.js:388, set in actCamp (bots.js:571), in actEngage at bots.js:686 `inp.crouch = seen && dist > 30 && Math.abs(inp.mz) < 0.1 && a.tier >= 3`, and by the sniper branch at bots.js:698. Consumed at player.js:897 and paid off at royale.js:167 `if (st.crouching) spread *= CROUCH.spreadMult` (0.62). An AR bot holding 30-45 m now crouch-strafes at 0.45 speed for a 0.62 cone; net spread ~0.82× vs 1.45× standing-walk. Real, not decorative.
4. Difficulty scaling: PARTIALLY closed. bots.js:32 `ROOKIE_TIER_MIX = [18, 16, 10, 4, 1]` (sums to 49, verified) replaces `[8, 12, 14, 10, 5]` for the first three RECORDED matches — gate at bots.js:75. Combined tier-4+5 count drops 15 → 5. Verified live, not inert: W.progress is assigned at boot (hud.js:508 in showMenu, called from ffg_royale3d.js:525) before attachBrain runs (ffg_royale3d.js:361), and `p.career = newCareer(p.career)` (hud.js:1367) always yields a defined career. But it is first-run protection only — `grep -rni "difficulty|sbmm|skillEstimate|casual" runtime/` returns ZERO hits, so from match 4 onward every player forever gets the identical fixed mix.
5. Not in the prior gap list, but a genuine behavioural fix: bots.js:193 `s.FLEE = ... (heals ? 86 : 72)`. FLEE used to require `heals`, so a cracked bot with an empty bag scored 0 and stood trading until it died.

WHAT DID NOT MOVE:
- Shield top-off, the prior "critical". bots.js:194 is byte-identical to the line the prior scorecard quotes (diffed both revisions above). Actors still spawn `shield: 0` (player.js:56). At hp 100 / shield 0 the first clause needs hp<80 and the second needs hp<60, so a healthy bot carrying six minis scores HEAL = 0. Current asymmetry with a legendary AR (30 × 1.32 = 39.6 body): player breaks a bot's 100 EHP in 2.6 hits ≈ 0.5 s of continuous fire; a bot needs ~6 hits through a ~57% burst duty cycle ≈ 1.9 s through the player's 200 EHP. Still ~3.5-4× in the human's favour (prior estimated 4-6×; the headshot fix took the edge off, the dominant term is untouched).
- Pathfinding. `grep -rni "navmesh|pathfind|astar|waypoint" runtime/` → zero hits. moveToward (bots.js:444-461) is unchanged: straight-line steer, hop when support 1.4 m ahead is 0.55-2.2 m up (bots.js:454) against a jump apex of 7.8²/(2×22) = 1.38 m, and a stuck reroute to `randNear(W, a, 25)` at bots.js:458. Slightly WORSE in surface area now: maps.js:630-665 rebuilds previously-deleted underwater huts on stilts, each with one 1.4 m door and floor loot at deck+0.5 m — and its own comment records that Deepwood's Riverside Mill anchor is dry on ZERO of 2000 seeds, so those are net-new indoor loot rooms the bots cannot reliably enter.
- Cover-seeking. `losBlocked` appears exactly once in bots.js (line 249, inside perceive). The suppression reflex (bots.js:425-434) still picks a point 18 m out at the attacker's bearing ±1.2 rad with no occlusion test.
- Sniper lead. bots.js:645 `if (def.speed && def.speed < 600 ...)`; sniper speed is still 700 (royale.js:64). Unchanged one-character fix.
- Personality depth. rotator is still exactly two decisions (bots.js:106 hot-drop, bots.js:211 PUSH eligibility); loot_goblin gained one (SUPPLY 78 vs 58, bots.js:217) for a total of three. Still ~3 observable archetypes across a 49-bot lobby, not 6.
- Behavioural test coverage. royale.selftest.cjs:150-154 is still the same four arithmetic assertions (mixes sum to 49, name pool ≥ 60, tier 5 aims better than tier 1). ROOKIE_TIER_MIX is not asserted anywhere — it lives in bots.js and is never exported to sim/royale.js, so nothing would catch it if it stopped summing to 49 and the tier draw at bots.js:80 (`/ 49 * mix.reduce(...)`) skewed. A synchronous `fastForward` harness now exists (ffg_royale3d.js:537, drives botsMod.update at 1/30 s), but it is a browser-only `window.__LC__` hook with no test calling it.

CONTEXT SHIFT: net.js:5-11 cut the human cap from 8 to 4 (Supabase Realtime H² message billing). Bots are now 46 of 50 slots even in a full friend lobby — this dimension carries more of the product than it did at the prior score, not less.

justification:
Real movement, but none of it in the loot MODEL — the sim tables were not touched at all. `git diff 791b7806^ HEAD -- runtime/sim/royale.js` changes only Match/squad bookkeeping; CONSUMABLES (royale.js:94-99), LOOT_WEIGHTS (289-293) and RARITY_DMG_MULT/SPREAD (48-49) are byte-identical to the prior score. Verified by execution, not just reading: `node` require of the sim prints exactly four consumable ids (bandage, medkit, mini_shield, big_shield), 20,000 floor rolls yield 5,895 consumables of which 100% are heals, and mini_shield throughput is 12.50 shield/s against big_shield's 12.50 — the strict-dominance tie is untouched.

What DID move is four things at the edges. (1) The prompt no longer lies: hud.js:2205-2220 `interactLabel()` renders "[E] Swap for AR (epic) — drops SHTG", and "FULL — no room for X" for the three cases give() actually refuses (ammo, same-kind stack at max, weapon-swap off a non-gun slot at the 3-gun cap). It did not exist before — `git show 791b7806^:...hud.js | grep -c interactLabel` returns 0. That closes the highest-impact prior gap outright. (2) Bots now contest supply drops: bots.js:57-65 marks every alive bot within 220 m on supplyDropLanded and forces a re-think, bots.js:216-218 scores s.SUPPLY = (58, or 78 for loot_goblin) − 0.12/m with a 90 s expiry, routed at 298-299/413 into actSupply (497-506), which clears the mark on arrival and hands off to actLoot. Effective conversion radius is ~150 m, not 220 (58 − 0.12d beats ROTATE's 40 floor only inside 150 m; only ~133 m against a stale ENGAGE 42) — smaller catchment than the flag radius implies, but live and correct. (3) A loot-loop bug the prior score MISSED is fixed: at 791b7806^ `const target = near.find(n => !n.taken && (n.type === "chest" || items.has(n.id)))` plus nearby()'s distance sort meant any ground item nearer than a chest won the target every frame and the else-branch wiped chestChannel.t — the chest could never reach its 2.0 s open. hut() places a floor point (maps.js:663) and a 50% chest (664) within ~1-2 m of each other, so this fired constantly. loot.js:627-630 now uses a 0.18 s tap/hold discriminator. (4) Placement got honest at the generator: maps.js:612-613 loot()/chest() refuse any authored y below waterY+0.4 (the code's own 300-seed measurement: 64% of Palm Bay's, 40% of Lakeside Cabins' and 39% of Banana Farm's town chests were spawning under the sea), while keeping intentional over-water points (stilt hut at waterY+0.85/0.95, pier waterY+1.1); and per-chest ground sampling replaced POI-centre sampling at maps.js:1031/1264/1358/1397 (its own note: 27% of Meadow Farm's chests floated >1 m, worst 5.3 m). Death drops finally get a marker too — loot.js:540-541 attaches a 1.3-scale gold glow (chests use 3.2).

Against the six axes the prior entry named as fairly judgeable (consumables not 100% healing, heal cancellable, full-inventory prompt names the outgoing item, manual drop exists, chests audible, rarity beams on ground loot), the score goes from 0/6 to 1/6. The structure — 5 slots, 5-tier ladder, Fortnite's heal table, seeded source-derived ids, supply-drop pacing, full-kit death drops, 3D slot icons with I-V numerals — is unchanged and still holds parity with a polished browser BR. It is improved inside the parity band, not out of it, and it is still at the bottom of that band.

A PRIOR-SCORE ERROR I HAVE TO CORRECT — standard phase 1 is not a gap. The prior entry rated it "high impact" by comparing the wall's trailing edge (8.23 m/s, worst case 10.05) against the 9.6 m/s sprint. That comparison omits the 80-second WAIT before the shrink. Simulating the real Storm against the real spawn distribution (maps.js:1971-1978, uniform over +/-720 m, so max spawn distance 1018 m): standard phase-1 storm deaths are 0.0% over 500 seeds under straight-line rotation from landing, 0.0% even at swimSprint 5.6 m/s, and still only 8.6% for a player who ignores the storm until t=140 (60 s into the shrink). It is also structurally impossible to start outside standard's first circle — startRadiusFrac 1.35 x 784 = 1058 m > the 1018 m maximum spawn distance. Standard's pacing is sound; that gap should be struck from the scorecard, and this is a measurement correction, not code movement.

WHAT IS REAL, UNFIXED, AND NOW POINTED AT NEW PLAYERS — quick phase 1. Same simulator, 500 seeds each: 5.8% die under perfect play (beeline from t=0, zero looting); 28.2% die if they start rotating at t=20, which is exactly when the game's own 10-second warning fires (storm.js:105-108); 44.6% die if they loot through the 30 s wait — which is the mode's advertised purpose. Binary-searched over 40 seeds, the maximum survivable spawn distance at the moment that warning fires averages 691 m against a 1018 m maximum spawn distance: roughly 28% of the spawn square is outside it. The warning system gives 10 seconds of notice for a wall that needs about 40 seconds of head start. Bots are unaffected — bots.js:204-207 scores ROTATE 95 from t=0 for anyone that far out, above ENGAGE — so this kills the human and not the lobby. And hud.js:641-670 now sorts QUICK to the first card for any player with zero career matches, pre-selects it, and badges it "START HERE · FIGHTING IN 10 SECONDS". Before this program a rookie's first match was standard (provably safe); it is now the mode carrying the one critical defect. justification:
The two gaps the prior entry called CRITICAL are closed at the generator level, and I verified both in the current source plus by replicating the generators in Node.

(1) "No structure can be fought FROM." Every enterable generator now carries a real aperture. house() (maps.js:919-939) cuts a 1.2 m x 1.1 m window in BOTH side walls — sill spans y+0.00..1.20 (line 929), header y+2.30..3.40 (line 930) — and adds a second door in the back wall (923-925). hut() got the identical band (maps.js:650-657). tower()'s upper-floor band was moved onto the eyeline: SILL_H 1.40 at fy+0.70 and HEAD_H 1.50 at fy+3.25 (maps.js:698-699), so the opening is fy+1.40..fy+2.50. Standing eye sits inside the aperture, crouched eye (0.97 / fy+1.27) is below the sill, and a 1.38 m jump apex puts the capsule at 1.38..3.18 which overlaps the header, so blockedHoriz (player.js:713) still refuses passage. It is a firing port, not a hole. Previously the tower band sat 0.88 m ABOVE the tallest eyeline in the game and houses had zero apertures.

(2) "Isla Viva's POIs are under water." snapPoiToLand + dryFrac (maps.js:797-816) run on the five inland POIs before anything is built (maps.js:1213-1216). Replicating them verbatim over 8 seeds: every snapped POI centre goes from -3.8..+2.0 m to +1.2..+6.3 m and from 0-48% dry to 60-100% dry, mean move 20-220 m. town() also retries the setback outward through [1, 1.5, 2.1, 2.7] (maps.js:997-1001): house build rate over 100 seeds is Palm Bay 72%, Jungle Market 69%, Coco Village 89%, Lakeside Cabins 97% (prior audit measured Palm Bay 0/8 houses on 4 of 8 seeds). loot()/chest() now refuse anything below waterY+0.4 (maps.js:612-613) and chests sample their OWN ground instead of the POI centre (maps.js:1029-1032, 1192-1195, 1357-1359, 1395-1398).

Cover density — the "high" gap — is fixed and I measured it independently, not from the comments. Replicating the stratified scatter (maps.js:769-779) with the real height functions and the post-snap POI list, over 4 seeds per map: Ashgrid 862 solid-collider props (prior audit: 318-327), Deepwood 966 (prior: 851-867), Isla Viva 242 (prior: 129-141). Mean distance from open ground (outside POI circles, above water) to the nearest solid cover is 23.2 m Isla Viva / 23.2 m Ashgrid / 21.9 m Deepwood, with 9.8% / 9.0% / 6.7% of open ground more than 40 m from cover. The prior entry's 54-90 m mean prop spacing is gone.

Against Final Drop — which HAS building, so its map does not have to supply cover while Last Circle's must — the map now carries its own weight: enterable, shootable-from structures everywhere, cover at ~22 m, three maps with guaranteed biome zones, sky islands + portals, a live contest-heat drop screen. That is parity. It is not "ahead", because one of the three maps still ships two seed-dependent defects a polished product would not (final circle at sea; POI circles overlapping), foliage still does not block, and several outlying POIs are still one or two structures.

Re-measured live this session on the SAME hardware the prior score used (ANGLE / NVIDIA RTX A2000 Laptop, D3D11, WebGL 2.0), same map and seed (Deepwood 424242), same 1280x720, medium tier, via a local server and direct renderer.info reads. Numbers below are prior -> now.

FRAME COST, ground third-person view: 763 draw calls / 3,716,659 tris / 12.6 ms -> 358 calls / 2,361,925 tris / 5.19 ms. Heaviest frame (50 actors clustered in view): 1,010 calls / 4,456,503 tris / 17.77 ms -> 424 calls / 2,821,168 tris / 8.46 ms. Camera at empty sky: 2,901,932 tris -> 1,801,341 tris in 61 calls. Ashgrid ground view now 388 calls / 6.86 ms.
